source.title: Grokking From Abstraction to Intelligence
source.authors: Jun-Jie Zhang; Zhen Shen; Gang Xiong; Xi-Song Dong

record.file_problem: No file problem; the full paper text is present. The text does contain internal inconsistencies noted under problems.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains models on modular arithmetic and reports train/test accuracy over training, directly measuring delayed generalization; it uses a different model configuration and adds structural analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes from its own modular-arithmetic experiments. It also describes proposed sweeps, including an SFM β=0 ablation, without giving their outcomes; those descriptions are not recorded as results. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: Not an original source. It trains Transformers (48-layer GPT-2 style plus a 2-layer baseline) on modular arithmetic mod 97 with a 50/50 split. It reports memorization followed by delayed generalization (Fig. 1, Sec. 4, B.5) and tracks mechanistic progress measures (BDM, spectral Gini/IPR, CMS, ablations, persistent homology) across checkpoints. Those results bear on V1, V2 and, narrowly, V6. The SFM is a hand-built surrogate with an explicit sparsity penalty, so its transition is induced by design and is not evidence on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that grokking in modular arithmetic is a spontaneous structural simplification (Occam's razor/MDL). Memorization corresponds to a high-complexity redundant state, and generalization emerges abruptly, not incrementally, when complexity collapses and Fourier/circular structure forms. They present the SFM as a hypothesis-generating surrogate, not a derivation of SGD dynamics, and also claim it shows grokking can arise in non-neural architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular arithmetic and train/test accuracy, but uses a 48-layer GPT-2-style model, a 50%/50% split, and multiple operations; it adds longitudinal causal, spectral, and complexity analyses rather than reproducing only the original setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports changes with model depth, weight-decay strength, modulus, and BDM quantization/block-size choices. Stronger weight decay changes the magnitude of spectral concentration; the transition pattern is reported across tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking time grows with the prime modulus (≈p^2.2 in text, p^2.51 in the figure fit), and the Gini onset is delayed for larger p.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking delay scales polynomially with task size (modulus) at a fixed train fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: A hand-designed spectral surrogate with an explicit L0 penalty shows a sharp memorization-to-sparse crossover, and its theoretical n* correlates with Transformer grokking steps across p.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An explicit complexity-penalized surrogate reproduces grokking-like transitions and calibrates to Transformer grokking times.

fits_no_version.finding: Layers with the largest BDM drop have the largest causal contribution (R² ≈ 0.88 in prose, 0.98 in the figure heading), apparently measured on a 12-layer model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise simplification predicts layer-wise causal importance in grokked networks.

record.problems: Many reported outcomes are qualitative or figure-based without exact values. The text gives conflicting values for the modulus scaling exponent (p²·² versus p²·⁵¹) and the layer-correlation R² (≈ 0.88 in prose versus ≈ 0.98 in a figure heading). Appendix B.3 refers to a 12-layer model despite the main experimental description specifying a 48-layer model and a 2-layer shallow baseline. The paper itself notes that the SFM is hand-designed and not derived from Transformer SGD; it also says optimizer/schedule/model-size baselines are incomplete.
record.rows_left_out: Not separately rowed: supplementary comparisons of BDM with block entropy, spectral entropy, effective rank, nuclear norm, and stable rank; BDM quantization/block-size robustness; and several spectral null baselines. These are described as corroborating complexity-proxy behavior but add no distinct result for the listed claim versions beyond the complexity-transition and controls already recorded. The stated β=0 SFM ablation has no reported outcome in the text.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only a 50% split is used).
Whether progress measures anticipate the jump (only four checkpoints; measures move in the same window). Circuit-level account for × and ÷.
All: no non-algorithmic data, no initialization-scale manipulation.
All: the 48-layer model is trained only on modular arithmetic, despite the authors' 'scalable to LLMs' framing.
Empirically all: no training-set-size sweep, no critical size or ungrokking in trained networks. The weight-decay sweep outcomes on grokking are not reported.
Algorithm identity across architectures or hyperparameters; deep vs shallow are compared only on BDM and accuracy.
All: no optimizer or floating-point controls; the authors list optimizer comparisons as future work.

missing.what: Outcomes of the weight-decay sweep (grokking onset and fraction of runs that grok at wd 0/0.1/1), plus the LR, warmup and batch sweeps. Table 4 says these are reported, but no results appear.
SFM β=0 ablation outcome (described, not reported)
Numeric train/test accuracies at the 1k/10k/100k checkpoints and mean±std across seeds
Layer-wise ΔBDM vs CMS correlation (R² 0.88 vs 0.98 conflict)

record.verdict_notes: Credibility concerns a researcher should weigh. Many appendix figures use 0–100 'training steps (log scale proxy)' axes and look schematic. The text and figures give conflicting values (p^2.2 vs p^2.51; R² 0.88 vs 0.98). B.3 and B.9 refer to a 12-layer model (layers L0–L11) despite the 48-layer setup. Sec. 4 mentions a parameter count 'beyond 1.5B', which is implausible for 48 layers at d=512. Table 4 lists sweeps 'reported' without results. Appendix text responds to 'the reviewer's intuition'. The intro's claim of continuous early KC decrease contradicts Sec. 4's BDM plateau. All results are on one modular-arithmetic setup with AdamW; V3, V4 and V7 are untested.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled sweep of training-set size is reported, so the claim that smaller training sets require more optimization is not tested.

The paper does not give a full circuit-level account for multiplication and division; it describes the SFM’s diagonal-support account as most directly applicable to addition/subtraction. It does not directly establish that its measured progress metrics reliably predict the accuracy jump in advance.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale sweep is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.

The low-complexity-bias account is implemented in the SFM surrogate, not established as the cause in SGD-trained Transformers. No empirical training-set-size sweep or observed ungrokking below a critical size is reported.
The paper reports cross-seed consistency of high-scoring heads, but does not compare identified algorithms across architectures or hyperparameters.
No controlled test of adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax floating-point limits is reported.

rows.subject: Singular Feature Machine (SFM) surrogate
rows.size_stated: Spectral weight matrix W ∈ C^(p×p); p = 97 in the main task formulation
rows.operation_detail: Apply spectral drift followed by an explicit sparsity-based Occam Gate

conditions.value: modular arithmetic; diagonal Fourier-support account most directly for addition/subtraction
sharp crossover in the SFM surrogate

rows.measure: Generalization-like transition and active spectral support
rows.baseline: Dense, high-entropy memorization-like regime
rows.value: The surrogate is described as transitioning to a sparse structured support as the Occam Gate prunes weights; its proxy complexity changes from O(p²) to O(p).
rows.note: This is a designed surrogate with an explicit complexity penalty, not an observed derivation of SGD behavior in the Transformer.
rows.check: The SFM transition is induced by an explicit β ln n·||W||0 penalty and hard threshold. This is a designed surrogate, not a measurement of a trained network's bias, so it does not test V5.

rows.subject: Singular Feature Machine (SFM) surrogate
rows.operation_detail: Derive a critical sample size by equating the surrogate free-energy expressions
rows.baseline: Memorization and generalization surrogate free energies
rows.value: An implicit critical-size equation and Lambert-W expression for n* are given; the paper reports a strong linear correlation between predicted n* and observed Transformer grokking steps.
rows.uncertainty: The correlation is described as strong; no numeric correlation coefficient is stated in the text.
rows.note: The paper does not report a dataset-size sweep or observed ungrokking below n*; it explicitly calls the SFM a surrogate.
rows.check: n* is a theoretical function of p, correlated with grokking steps across moduli. No training-set-size sweep and no ungrokking are reported. A stated R² > 0.95 appears only in the figure heading.

rows.subject: Transformer models, aggregate across tested moduli
rows.operation_detail: Measure grokking time across prime moduli
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: The text reports tg scaling approximately as p²·²; Figure 13a also labels a fit as tg ∝ p²·⁵¹.
rows.note: This varies modulus, not training-set size; the two reported scaling exponents conflict.
rows.check: The modulus sweep at a fixed 50% fraction does not vary training-set size relative to the task, so it cannot test V1's dataset-size dependence. The exponents conflict (p^2.2 in text vs p^2.51 in the figure fit).
